en.text:
Shirou Kuniuji Ashikaga—Moriuji's legitimate grandson. Supreme commander of Rokuhara.
Use that boy as the key to making Rokuhara disappear...?

What had the captain intended?
Certainly, the occupation wanted to destroy the Rokuhara administration inside the castle, not the castle for its own sake. If Rokuhara no longer existed, there would be no need to drop the bomb. The reasoning itself was sound.

The Green Dragon Society behind them might not care whether Rokuhara existed. But it did not control the occupation forces; it only steered them cleverly. It could not simply ignore their interests. If the shogunate vanished, the plan would stall.

A shogunate, however, is not a thing one creates and removes just like that.

The captain's message was too brief for me to see her real intention.

Probably she had given only the essentials to spare Muramasa, unfamiliar with modern affairs, the explanation from beginning to end.
A considerate economy. At present I resented every word it had saved.

Wait. No. ◆

Shirou Kuniuji Ashikaga is the key?

Assassinate him, the supreme commander?
No. Not that. Not that at all.

He was far too young to bear Rokuhara upon his shoulders and held no real power at present.
His disappearance would not destroy it.

So not kill him.
Keep him alive.

His presence was not vital to Rokuhara's practical functioning. His loss would not deal the shogunate a mortal wound.
But he could bring the shogunate to an end.

Give up the government.
Ask him to announce the end of Rokuhara as the body governing the nation.

Kuniuji Ashikaga was only the nominal head of the shogunate.
But nominal or not, he was its head. An official declaration made in his name would carry immense significance—at least until those with actual power repudiated it.

The occupation had judged Rokuhara an illegitimate government and sent its troops to remove it.
So we would do exactly what they asked. Before they could. By Rokuhara's own action.

Then the occupation would lose its reason to continue fighting.

Of course, it could ignore the announcement.
But the cost would be immense: the loss of its righteous-war banner, damage to its standing with Yamato's people, international criticism, and more.

Whoever directed the occupation—whether the British Commonwealth or the New Continent independence faction—would surely find that unacceptable.
They might lose every benefit of the war.

This could stop the forged thunderbomb!
If Kuniuji Ashikaga himself declared the Rokuhara order finished!

　国家統治機構としての六波羅の終焉を表明するよう
願う。

　足利邦氏は名目上の幕府元首に過ぎない。
　だが名目上でも首長であるからには、その名のもと
公的宣言がなされれば、重大な意義を持つだろう……
少なくとも、実権を握る者に否定されるまでの間は。

　進駐軍は六波羅を不当な政府と断定し、この排除を
名分として兵を動かした。
　だから――彼らの言う通りにしてやるのだ。先手を
打って、六波羅自身の行動で。

　そうなっては進駐軍は戦闘続行する理由を失なくす。

　黙殺するのは勿論、可能だ。
　だがその場合、正義の戦争という看板の喪失、大和
国民の心象への悪影響、国際社会の批判等々、失う物
が多過ぎる。

　それは進駐軍を動かす者――大英連邦であれ新大陸
独立派であれ――にとって受け入れ難いはずだ。
　戦争利益を全て失いかねない。

　この方法なら、鍛造雷弾投下を止められる！
　足利邦氏の口で六波羅体制の終結を宣言させれば！

Broadcasting the announcement... the military wide-area channel would do.
It would carry the declaration too far and too widely for any cover-up.

The difficulty was, naturally, persuasion.

I had lived in Fudaraku Castle for a while, but my rank was only lieutenant colonel in the Dragon Army. Meeting an exalted personage like Kuniuji Ashikaga was not an opportunity that came my way.
Naturally, we had never spoken.

...Meaning.
I had to barge in upon a nobleman I had never met, and get him to agree to an outrageous demand.
An excellent foundation for confidence. Nothing was built upon it.
